latest_commit.subject: plan: sample deltas are phase quantisation, not a health signal (§1b)
latest_commit.body:
Adds the 2026-08-02 finding to the stall-discriminator plan.

Owner hypothesis "deltas >3 s coincide with a flush cycle continuing
into the 5-minute pre-sample flush" is REFUTED: the pump was PARKED at
42/42 preloads with a determinable state, because the flush cycle
restarts after each sample and is therefore phase-locked to the 53-min
schedule (every preload landed 100-148 s into the 8-min REST).
Independent phases would have caught a RUN in ~20 % of samples.

The deltas are one-revolution phase quantisation: spin-up (19.4 s) and
revolution period (16.0 s) are IDENTICAL between the delta<=3 (n=34)
and delta>3 (n=9) groups; the big-delta samples just took one extra
revolution (26 vs 25). Loading requires 7 crossings after scheduled_at
and sampled_at is the first of them, so delta wraps: +15 s means a
crossing missed the schedule by ~1 s. Added to non-goals: never use
delta as a pump-health signal (an earlier mid-run reading of the +15 s
cluster as battery decline was wrong).

What it contributes to hypothesis (b): across 43 loading windows the
inter-crossing intervals were uniform 15-17 s with ZERO intervals
>=24 s — ~1,075 consecutive hall crossings with no dropped
registration. So the hall path is demonstrably healthy in the TRIGGER
context and any blindness is episodic, not systemic. This does NOT
refute (b) — the stalls were in the flush-cycle BP_RUNNING context —
but Experiment 2 must now reproduce the FLUSH-RUN context specifically
(2-min RUN / 8-min REST, CPU napping between hall wakes) or it will
re-measure the healthy path and produce a false negative.

Status updated: the board is free (run ended on battery exhaustion).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
